newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALBAK TO RETAIN PACKAGING AFTER UNBUNDLING.
newsitem.headline: MALBAK TO RETAIN PACKAGING AFTER UNBUNDLING.

text.p: South African conglomerate Malbak Ltd said on Thursday it would retain its packaging units Kohler and London-listed MY Holdings following an unbundling of the company.
It added it was currently considering conditional offers for its Malbak Motor, Defy and ICL units.
The firm said the moves would leave it as a packaging group with a market capitalisation of more than two billion rand and more than 30 percent of its earnings originating offshore.
Malbak added that was in talks with Haggie and Osborn MMD with regard to the pre-emptive rights in respect of the shares in those two firms.
Malbaks' listed subsidiaries of Ellerine Holdings , Foodcorp , New Clicks Holdings and SA Druggists, will be distributed to shareholders.
This will occur on the basis of 13,950 Ellerine shares, 11,216 Foodcorp shares, 37,763 New clicks shares and 16,490 SA Druggists shares for every 100 Malbak shares held.
Along with the share distribution will come a cash distribution -- including an interim dividend -- from the proceeds of the sale of all Malbak's unlisted firms and its interest in Haggie.

Electrolux of Sweden has been rumoured to be interested in placing a bid for Defy with one Swedish newspaper report valuing such a move at between 320 and 480 million crowns (200 to 300 million rand).
The sale of all unlisted investments, which also includes Malbak Motor Holdings, ICL (SA) and Amalgamated Appliances, is expected to exceed 700 million rand.
The disposals by Malbak of its unlisted subsidiaries form part of the group's decision to unbundle its assets in a bid to unlock the value of its underlying investments.
Once the unbundling is completed Malbak will own 68 percent of Kohler and 64 percent of MY, giving it sales of 2.8 billion rand.

Malbak said a shareholders' meeting will be held on March 24 to approve of the proposals. Provided approval is given and a number of regulatory requirements are met the unbundling will become unconditional on April 25.
